text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- RISK OF BANKING SECTOR IS LOWER IN BRAZIL

The risk rating of Brazil's banking sector is improving, according to Francisco Abreu, analyst at Moody's Investors Service rating agency. Moody's will release a full report on the Brazilian banking sector next Wednesday.
Brazilian state-owned telecommunications holding firm Telebras said it had a record net profit of 3.254 billion reais. Telebras' net consolidated profit was 2.756 billion reais.
The holding's net earnings rose 175 percent when compared with a 1.183 billion reais net profit in 1995.
-- MONETARY COUNCIL TO REGULATE CREDIT TO STATE BANKS
Brazil's National Monetary Council (CMN) is likely to announce today regulations regarding credit lines created last year to facilitate the privatization of state banks.
-- FOUR FIRMS LEAD FRAUD SCHEME WITH BONDS

A congressional inquiry into irregularities with the dealing of municipal and state bonds has found that four companies led the fraud scheme that drained 600 million reais from states and municipalities.
-- CENTRAL BANK SUSPENDS DEALING OF STATE, MUNICIPAL BONDS

Brazil's Central Bank has suspended trade with securities issued by states and municipalities. The decision followed a request from a parliamentary inquiry committee looking into a multi-million fraud scheme involving state and municipal bonds.
-- POLICE FREE DRUG DEALER FOR LACK OF MEDICAL TREATMENT
A judge ordered the police to free a drug dealer because he was not given proper medical treatment when he was arrested last year after being shot by policemen.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
